set.tagline: A missing brother, a security cyborg, and Louisiana's industrial swamps after dark.
set.description: NORCO Act One is the free first act of Geography of Robots' Southern Gothic point-and-click adventure. Follow a missing-person trail through refineries, drainage ditches and suburban New Orleans before deciding whether to buy the full story.

systemRequirements.min: GOG lists Windows 7 and 4 GB RAM for the free Act One release. GOG offers a macOS build but does not publish a separate Mac CPU, RAM, graphics or storage breakdown for this demo.
systemRequirements.recommended: No separate recommended tier is published on the Act One GOG page. Requirements for the later full NORCO release should not be silently copied onto this demo.

min.notes: 4 GB RAM and Windows 7 are GOG's listed Windows minimum for Act One. A Mac build exists; its distinct numerical minimum is not specified on the Act One listing.

recommended.notes: GOG does not give a separate recommended specification for this free act.

set.launcherInstall.note: Free DRM-free GOG Act One for Windows and macOS. Add it to a GOG library, download the offline build for your OS, and install or locate it. This is not the paid full NORCO game. A one-click PlayBound package has not been verified.

qualityBar.verdict: A free first chapter that makes a refinery feel like a family secret you were never meant to read.

set.longDescription:
NORCO Act One starts with an absence. Your brother Blake is missing after your mother's death, and the trail leads through a version of South Louisiana where oil refineries, damp neighborhoods and strange technology share the same horizon. The game is a point-and-click narrative adventure, but its most immediate hook is the place. Industrial towers and flooded streets are drawn in painterly pixel art that makes an ordinary strip mall seem as loaded with history as a ruined temple.

Geography of Robots released this first act free before the full NORCO arrived. The Act One GOG listing still contains old coming-soon copy about the complete game. That copy should not become PlayBound's description: the full release is a separate, paid purchase, and this page is for the limited free opening. You can use the act to see whether its writing, pace and setting pull you in without buying the rest of the story first. The trail involves a fugitive security cyborg and the aftermath of a family loss, but the pleasure is in examining the spaces between those plot points. A drainage ditch or refinery wall can tell you as much about this world as a conversation.

The game is single-player and built around pointing, clicking and reading. Steam lists full controller support for the later complete NORCO release, but that does not verify the older free Act One GOG package. We are keeping a controller badge off this draft until that exact build is tested or a PlayBound Controls profile is made. There is no native online mode, virtual LAN use case or dedicated server to wire. PlayBound parties should not be advertised for a solitary first chapter.

GOG offers Windows and macOS versions of Act One as DRM-free downloads; Galaxy is optional. Its Act One page gives a Windows 7 and 4 GB RAM minimum, but no full per-platform hardware sheet or separate recommended tier. The full NORCO Steam page lists more detailed specifications, yet they are for a different release. Keeping those figures separate is more useful than copying a plausible-looking CPU or GPU into a demo's requirement card. Likewise, the older Draft's 2026 release year is wrong: GOG dates this act to August 2021.

Act One is a good way to decide whether you want to spend more time in NORCO's world. It is deliberately a beginning, with the boundaries that entails. The memorable part is how a search for one missing person makes an entire industrial landscape feel implicated. If that first trip through the swamps stays with you, the complete game is there when you are ready.
set.whyWePickedIt: Act One offers a free way into one of PC adventure gaming's most distinctive settings. The writing and pixel art make South Louisiana feel specific, strange and lived-in. We keep the entry honest as an opening chapter, with the full game a separate purchase and its controller claims unverified for this build.
set.thatOneThing: Your missing-person lead is a fugitive security cyborg, and somehow the refinery still feels like the more suspicious witness.

installSteps.text: Add the free NORCO Act One release to your GOG library. Download its Windows offline installer, run it, then use PlayBound Locate if you want to track the existing install.
Add NORCO Act One to your GOG library for free, download the macOS build listed for this act, and follow the installation directions included with that GOG package.
Start Act One from your installed copy. This is the opening chapter, not the full paid NORCO game.

firstPlaySteps.text: Examine rooms and talk to people before moving on. The details of each place carry much of the story.

faq.a: Yes. GOG offers the first act free. The complete NORCO game is a separate paid release.

faq.q: Does Act One include the whole story?
faq.a: No. It is the opening act and ends before the complete game's story is finished.
Controller support is documented for the later full NORCO release on Steam, but the free Act One GOG build has not been verified. Use mouse input for this listing.

faq.a: No multiplayer mode is listed for this single-player story act.
GOG lists Windows and macOS downloads for Act One. Galaxy is optional.
